text: DSH Plugin Updates 是面向 DSH Web 的插件更新检查器。它读取当前 profile 中的插件依赖，按 npm、GitHub、发布包和本地链接等来源检查可用版本，并结合运行中的 DSH 核心版本判断兼容状态。Web 侧边栏提供更新列表、状态徽标、立即检查、忽略版本和暂缓提醒，设置页可配置检查周期与来源；agent 工具提供只读检查结果，更新由用户自行决定。可选 GitHub 认证使用用户指定的环境变量。

DSH Plugin Updates checks DSH Web plugin versions against the running core. Its sidebar lists results with check, ignore and snooze controls. Settings configure checks, and a read-only agent tool reports findings. Users decide whether to apply updates. GitHub token setup is optional.
想知道 DSH profile 里的插件有没有新版本，并确认是否兼容当前核心。
给 DSH 加一个侧边栏页面，集中查看插件更新状态。
I want to check which installed DSH plugins have newer versions that fit my current core.
DSH Plugin Updates 的功能「版本兼容检查」：扫描 profile 插件依赖，检查 npm、GitHub、release 和本地来源的候选版本，并对照当前 DSH 核心显示兼容状态。
DSH Plugin Updates 查询 npm 和 GitHub 版本时会发送 profile 中的包名、版本或仓库信息；GitHub 令牌可选，从设置指定的环境变量读取。
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates 提供工具 PHONE_SIGNATURE_INVALID
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates 提供工具 PLUPD_PACKAGE_UNKNOWN
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates 提供工具 PLUPD_INTERNAL

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · dsh-plugin-updates：[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates)

An update checker that only offers plugin releases your running DSH core can actually load.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-better-sidebar   # the tab host, skip if installed
dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates

section: restart dsh web, then open the Updates tab

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · restart dsh web, then open the Updates tab：> **npm name.** The bare name `dsh-plugin-updates` is already taken on npm by an unrelated data package, so this plugin is published as `@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates`. The loader row id stays `plugin-updates` either way.
section: restart dsh web, then open the Updates tab

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Why：1. **Name collisions.** Many local plugins are `link:` folders or GitHub installs whose names also exist on npm as unrelated projects. A checker that looks packages up by name reports false "updates" and, if you approve, installs somebody else's package. This plugin classifies every dependency by its **specifier** (`^1.2.0`, `link:`, `github:`, a release tarball URL), never by its bare name.
2. **Wrong-core builds.** The newest release of a plugin often needs a newer DSH core than the one you run. Installing it can blank the whole web UI. This plugin applies the same compatibility rule as the DSH 0.2.1 loader against the **running** core version, so a 0.2.x-only build is never offered to a 0.1.5 host.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Why：It also keeps a list of holds (versions you know to avoid), per package notes, and gives you a memory-capped apply command to copy, because a bare `pnpm add` on a busy machine can exhaust memory.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · What you get：- An **Updates** tab in the sidebar (needs `dsh-better-sidebar`, optional) with a live count badge, grouped results, links (npm, releases, changelog, compare), **Check now**, **Ignore this version**, **Snooze** and **Copy command**.
- A **Settings** section for the options below.
- A read-only agent tool `plugin_updates` (and `plugin_updates_doctor`).
- `GET /dsh-plugin-updates/api/doctor` and a bundled doctor skill.
- Zero configuration: defaults work as installed.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · then restart dsh web: the server half loads at start only：```

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in `dsh.profile.bundles`. A local checkout works too: clone it, run `npm install --omit=dev` in it, then `dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-updates`. Requires Node 22.5 or newer and DSH 0.1.5-rc.1 up to (not including) 0.3.0. The browser half hot-reloads; only the server half needs the restart.
section: then restart dsh web: the server half loads at start only

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · then restart dsh web: the server half loads at start only：Kill switch without uninstalling: add `- id: plugin-updates` with `disabled: true` to the profile `cordis.patch.yml`, or set `DSH_PLUGIN_UPDATES_DISABLE=1`.
section: then restart dsh web: the server half loads at start only

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：Settings live in the `dsh-plugin-updates` namespace on DSH 0.1.5 (Settings page, stored in `settings.yaml`) and in the `plugin-updates` row of the profile `cordis.patch.yml` on DSH 0.2.x (settings forms). The plugin imports an old `settings.yaml` section once.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `intervalHours` | `12` | Hours between automatic checks (minimum 1). |
| `initialDelaySeconds` | `60` | Delay of the first check after start. After a restart the next check respects the last one, so restarts do not cause extra requests. |
| `registry` | `https://registry.npmjs.org` | Registry base URL. Must be on the host allowlist. |
| `allowHosts` | `[]` | Extra hosts, explicit opt-in only. |
| `githubTokenEnv` | `""` | The **name** of an environment variable that holds a GitHub token. Never the token. It is sent only to `api.github.com` and never stored or logged. |
| `channels` | `["latest"]` | Extra dist-tags to show (for example `next`). Never counted in the badge. |
| `holds` | seeded | Package name to a semver range to avoid. A value may end in `when dsh <range>` to apply only on some cores, for example `">=0.3.2 when dsh <0.2.0-0"`. |
| `upstream` | seeded | Local plugin (folder or package name) to `owner/repo`, or `owner/repo@<base>` to record the base version. Used for `link:` and `file:` plugins that are forks or clones. |
| `notes` | see

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：Seeded `holds` and `upstream` come from a manual audit of real plugins: they encode knowledge that registry metadata cannot carry (a desktop-only 0.2.x line, stepping-stone builds, an archived upstream). Replace them freely.
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · How it decides compatibility：The badge counts `update-compatible` only.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)：For a safe update the result carries `applyHint`, for example:

```bash
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u) systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1500M -p MemorySwapMax=0 \
  pnpm --dir "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/web" add --save-exact --ignore-scripts <package>@<version>
```
section: Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)：The cap makes a runaway install kill only itself. Check `free -m` first. Git and release tarball dependencies get the matching `pnpm add 'name@github:owner/repo#ref'` or release URL form. Local forks get a manual hint (rebase onto the upstream tag), because no package manager command applies. Add `afterInstall` reminders for packages that need a follow-up step. The agent tool says the same: do not run `pnpm add`, `pnpm update` or `dsh plugin add` on your own; present the list and let the human decide.
section: Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Agent tool and routes：`plugin_updates { scope?, package?, refresh? }` with `scope` one of `actionable` (default), `outdated`, `safe`, `held`, `local`, `all`. Read-only. `refresh: true` runs a new check (60 second cooldown).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Agent tool and routes：Routes under `/dsh-plugin-updates/api`: `GET status`, `GET list?scope=`, `GET detail?pkg=`, `GET doctor`, `GET health`, `GET settings`, `POST refresh`, `POST ignore {pkg,version?}`, `POST unignore {pkg}`, `POST snooze {pkg,days?}`, `POST settings {patch}`. POSTs require the header `X-Requested-With: dsh-plugin-updates`, a JSON body, a matching `Origin` and a loopback connection (or the host connection admission when it offers one). None of them touches anything except the plugin's own state file.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Privacy：- Only two hosts are ever contacted: **registry.npmjs.org** and **api.github.com**. Redirects to any other host are refused. `allowHosts` is an explicit opt-in that is empty by default.
- No telemetry, no catalog download, no mirrors, no analytics.
- The only data sent is package names, versions and repository names from your own profile, the same data `npm view` would send.
- Responses are cached with ETags in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-updates/state.json` (mode 0600), never in the profile. Registry and GitHub text is never shown or given to the model: only validated version strings and links the plugin builds itself.
- Unauthenticated GitHub access allows 60 requests per hour. A sweep of a large profile needs roughly 30 requests with ETags. The plugin stops below 10 remaining and reports the rest as `unreachable` until the reset.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · When something goes wrong：- Ask your agent to load the **`plugin-updates-doctor`** skill (bundled; see [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#start-here) if it is not listed).
- Run the self-check: `GET /dsh-plugin-updates/api/doctor` (no secrets in the output).
- Every error carries a stable `code`: [docs/ERRORS.md](docs/ERRORS.md).

The skill is registered automatically at the next `dsh web` start. Manual fallback:

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · When something goes wrong：```bash
P=$(node -p "require('path').dirname(require.resolve('dsh-plugin-updates/package.json',{paths:[(process.env.DSH_HOME||require('os').homedir()+'/.dsh')+'/profiles/web']}))")
mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && cp -r "$P/skills/plugin-updates-doctor" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"
```

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Development：```bash
npm install          # dev dependencies: esbuild, react, react-dom, jsdom
npm run build        # bundles src/client.jsx to lib/client.js, verifies it loads like the browser loader does
npm test             # unit tests with mocked HTTP, fake 0.1.5 and 0.2.1 contexts, jsdom client boot
DSH_GLOBAL_PREFIX=/path/to/a/dsh-0.2.x/prefix npm test   # same suite against another DSH line

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Development：`test/dry-eval.mjs` evaluates a read-only copy of a real profile against the live registry. Release history: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). License: MIT.

---
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · More plugins by the same author：All of them are open source and run on DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x (several on 0.1.5 too).

- `GET /dsh-plugin-updates/api/doctor` and a bundled doctor skill.

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in `dsh.profile.bundles`. text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：Settings live in the `dsh-plugin-updates` namespace on DSH 0.1.5 (Settings page, stored in `settings.yaml`) and in the `plugin-updates` row of the profile `cordis.patch.yml` on DSH 0.2.x (settings forms). The plugin imports an old `settings.yaml` section once.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `intervalHours` | `12` | Hours between automatic checks (minimum 1). |
| `initialDelaySeconds` | `60` | Delay of the first check after start. After a restart the next check respects the last one, so restarts do not cause extra requests. |
| `registry` | `https://registry.npmjs.org` | Registry base URL. Must be on the host allowlist. |
| `allowHosts` | `[]` | Extra hosts, explicit opt-in only. |
| `githubTokenEnv` | `""` | The **name** of an environment variable that holds a GitHub token. Never the token. It is sent only to `api.github.com` and never stored or logged. |
| `channels` | `["latest"]` | Extra dist-tags to show (for example `next`). Never counted in the badge. |
| `holds` | seeded | Package name to a semver range to avoid. A value may end in `when dsh <range>` to apply only on some cores, for example `">=0.3.2 when dsh <0.2.0-0"`. |
| `upstream` | seeded | Local plugin (folder or package name) to `owner/repo`, or `owner/repo@<base>` to record the base version. Used for `link:` and `file:` plugins that are forks or clones. |
| `notes` | see

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：Seeded `holds` and `upstream` come from a manual audit of real plugins: they encode knowledge that registry metadata cannot carry (a desktop-only 0.2.x line, stepping-stone builds, an archived upstream). Replace them freely.
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · How it decides compatibility：The badge counts `update-compatible` only.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)：For a safe update the result carries `applyHint`, for example:

```bash
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u) systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1500M -p MemorySwapMax=0 \
  pnpm --dir "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/web" add --save-exact --ignore-scripts <package>@<version>
```
section: Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)：The cap makes a runaway install kill only itself. Check `free -m` first. Git and release tarball dependencies get the matching `pnpm add 'name@github:owner/repo#ref'` or release URL form. Local forks get a manual hint (rebase onto the upstream tag), because no package manager command applies. Add `afterInstall` reminders for packages that need a follow-up step. The agent tool says the same: do not run `pnpm add`, `pnpm update` or `dsh plugin add` on your own; present the list and let the human decide.
section: Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Agent tool and routes：`plugin_updates { scope?, package?, refresh? }` with `scope` one of `actionable` (default), `outdated`, `safe`, `held`, `local`, `all`. Read-only. `refresh: true` runs a new check (60 second cooldown).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Agent tool and routes：Routes under `/dsh-plugin-updates/api`: `GET status`, `GET list?scope=`, `GET detail?pkg=`, `GET doctor`, `GET health`, `GET settings`, `POST refresh`, `POST ignore {pkg,version?}`, `POST unignore {pkg}`, `POST snooze {pkg,days?}`, `POST settings {patch}`. POSTs require the header `X-Requested-With: dsh-plugin-updates`, a JSON body, a matching `Origin` and a loopback connection (or the host connection admission when it offers one). None of them touches anything except the plugin's own state file.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Privacy：- Only two hosts are ever contacted: **registry.npmjs.org** and **api.github.com**. Redirects to any other host are refused. `allowHosts` is an explicit opt-in that is empty by default.
- No telemetry, no catalog download, no mirrors, no analytics.
- The only data sent is package names, versions and repository names from your own profile, the same data `npm view` would send.
- Responses are cached with ETags in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-updates/state.json` (mode 0600), never in the profile. Registry and GitHub text is never shown or given to the model: only validated version strings and links the plugin builds itself.
- Unauthenticated GitHub access allows 60 requests per hour. A sweep of a large profile needs roughly 30 requests with ETags. The plugin stops below 10 remaining and reports the rest as `unreachable` until the reset.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · When something goes wrong：- Ask your agent to load the **`plugin-updates-doctor`** skill (bundled; see [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#start-here) if it is not listed).
- Run the self-check: `GET /dsh-plugin-updates/api/doctor` (no secrets in the output).
- Every error carries a stable `code`: [docs/ERRORS.md](docs/ERRORS.md).

The skill is registered automatically at the next `dsh web` start. Manual fallback:

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · When something goes wrong：```bash
P=$(node -p "require('path').dirname(require.resolve('dsh-plugin-updates/package.json',{paths:[(process.env.DSH_HOME||require('os').homedir()+'/.dsh')+'/profiles/web']}))")
mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && cp -r "$P/skills/plugin-updates-doctor" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"
```

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Development：```bash
npm install          # dev dependencies: esbuild, react, react-dom, jsdom
npm run build        # bundles src/client.jsx to lib/client.js, verifies it loads like the browser loader does
npm test             # unit tests with mocked HTTP, fake 0.1.5 and 0.2.1 contexts, jsdom client boot
DSH_GLOBAL_PREFIX=/path/to/a/dsh-0.2.x/prefix npm test   # same suite against another DSH line

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Development：`test/dry-eval.mjs` evaluates a read-only copy of a real profile against the live registry. Release history: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). License: MIT.

| `upstream` | seeded | Local plugin (folder or package name) to `owner/repo`, or `owner/repo@<base>` to record the base version. Used for `link:` and `file:` plugins that are forks or clones. |
| `notes` | see

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Settings：Seeded `holds` and `upstream` come from a manual audit of real plugins: they encode knowledge that registry metadata cannot carry (a desktop-only 0.2.x line, stepping-stone builds, an archived upstream). Replace them freely.
@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · How it decides compatibility：The badge counts `update-compatible` only.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)：For a safe update the result carries `applyHint`, for example:

```bash
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u) systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1500M -p MemorySwapMax=0 \
  pnpm --dir "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/web" add --save-exact --ignore-scripts <package>@<version>
```
section: Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)：The cap makes a runaway install kill only itself. Check `free -m` first. Git and release tarball dependencies get the matching `pnpm add 'name@github:owner/repo#ref'` or release URL form. Local forks get a manual hint (rebase onto the upstream tag), because no package manager command applies. Add `afterInstall` reminders for packages that need a follow-up step. The agent tool says the same: do not run `pnpm add`, `pnpm update` or `dsh plugin add` on your own; present the list and let the human decide.
section: Applying an update (you do it, not the plugin)

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Agent tool and routes：`plugin_updates { scope?, package?, refresh? }` with `scope` one of `actionable` (default), `outdated`, `safe`, `held`, `local`, `all`. Read-only. `refresh: true` runs a new check (60 second cooldown).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Agent tool and routes：Routes under `/dsh-plugin-updates/api`: `GET status`, `GET list?scope=`, `GET detail?pkg=`, `GET doctor`, `GET health`, `GET settings`, `POST refresh`, `POST ignore {pkg,version?}`, `POST unignore {pkg}`, `POST snooze {pkg,days?}`, `POST settings {patch}`. POSTs require the header `X-Requested-With: dsh-plugin-updates`, a JSON body, a matching `Origin` and a loopback connection (or the host connection admission when it offers one). None of them touches anything except the plugin's own state file.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · Privacy：- Only two hosts are ever contacted: **registry.npmjs.org** and **api.github.com**. Redirects to any other host are refused. `allowHosts` is an explicit opt-in that is empty by default.
- No telemetry, no catalog download, no mirrors, no analytics.
- The only data sent is package names, versions and repository names from your own profile, the same data `npm view` would send.
- Responses are cached with ETags in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-updates/state.json` (mode 0600), never in the profile. Registry and GitHub text is never shown or given to the model: only validated version strings and links the plugin builds itself.
- Unauthenticated GitHub access allows 60 requests per hour. A sweep of a large profile needs roughly 30 requests with ETags. The plugin stops below 10 remaining and reports the rest as `unreachable` until the reset.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · When something goes wrong：- Ask your agent to load the **`plugin-updates-doctor`** skill (bundled; see [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#start-here) if it is not listed).
- Run the self-check: `GET /dsh-plugin-updates/api/doctor` (no secrets in the output).
- Every error carries a stable `code`: [docs/ERRORS.md](docs/ERRORS.md).

The skill is registered automatically at the next `dsh web` start. Manual fallback:

@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates README · When something goes wrong：```bash
P=$(node -p "require('path').dirname(require.resolve('dsh-plugin-updates/package.json',{paths:[(process.env.DSH_HOME||require('os').homedir()+'/.dsh')+'/profiles/web']}))")
mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && cp -r "$P/skills/plugin-updates-doctor" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"
```

npm run build        # bundles src/client.jsx to lib/client.js, verifies it loads like the browser loader does
